clue.text: Payment in advance of future production is welcomed by cosmetics expert in recession

definitions.text: Payment in advance of future production

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read from right to left
something welcomed by a host is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Estée Lauder founded the cosmetics company bearing her name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A make-up mogul in hard times accepts money up front for work not yet made.
explanation.walkthrough: Estée Lauder is the cosmetics expert. The definition refers to payments made before a work's later output earns, such as advances against royalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Residuals are royalty payments made to performers and creators tied to later showings or output of a work.

clue.text: Replants flamboyant trees around square

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the single letter for square
a flamboyant arrangement is showy and wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for square, as in sq or S on plans

explanation.surface: A gardener puts showy trees back in the ground around the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flamboyant' rearranges TREES, and 'around' places those letters about S.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a plant is to set it in the soil again, a gardening synonym for replanting.

clue.text: Students elevated in error

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: pupils are students at school

explanation.surface: Learners promoted by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' is a reversal signal in a down entry: PUPILS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a small mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Wife evenly adjusts heating system

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-numbered letters of the following word: second, fourth, sixth

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: A wife steadily tweaks the household boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'adjusts'. 'My old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife, from 'Duchess of Fife' rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney usage a man calls his spouse his 'old Dutch', so the word stands for a married partner.

clue.text: Art produced by rich RCA tutee?

indicators.note: produced here means made out of, so the following letters are reworked to make the answer

explanation.surface: Asks whether art made by a wealthy Royal College of Art student counts.
explanation.walkthrough: RCA is the Royal College of Art in London; its letters join RICH and TUTEE as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Designing buildings is counted among the fine arts, so the discipline is an art.

clue.text: Composer transposing parts in crib

indicators.note: swapping the two halves of the word puts its back part at the front

parts.note: a manger is a crib or feeding trough, as in the Nativity

explanation.surface: A musician moves sections around in a baby's cot.
explanation.walkthrough: MANGER split as MAN + GER becomes GER + MAN. Edward German was an English composer of light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward German wrote operettas such as Merrie England, making him a composer by surname.

clue.text: Include points on circuit

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
a compass can mean a circuit or boundary round something

explanation.surface: Take in the cardinal directions on a round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just links the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass something is to surround it and so contain or take it in.

clue.text: Bobby supporting staff for high-ranking official

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: to man is to staff a post
Bobby Darin was an American singer

explanation.surface: A policeman underpins the team on behalf of a senior civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a British policeman but is the singer Bobby Darin; 'supporting' puts DARIN under MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a senior Chinese civil servant, and the word now means any powerful bureaucrat.

clue.text: Being short of wrapping length is irritating

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped round the other, which goes inside

parts.note: needing something means lacking it

explanation.surface: Running out of gift wrap is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' puts L inside NEEDING; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means provoking or annoying someone with repeated jibes.

clue.text: A cat is nervous about managing a complaint

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, i.e. surround, the other piece
a nervous creature is jittery and agitated, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: IC means in charge, i.e. managing

explanation.surface: A jittery cat has a nervous condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' rearranges A CAT IS into SCIATA, and 'about' wraps that round IC (in charge).
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is a painful disorder of the nerve running down the leg, a medical ailment.

clue.text: Fine cake containing a bit of cinnamon

indicators.note: the cake holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: a scone is a small plain cake

indicators.note: a small bit of the word, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lovely bun with a dash of spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective praising the cake but is a noun: at Oxford a sconce was a forfeit imposed for breaches of table etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford colleges a sconce was a penalty, usually a tankard of ale, levied for a social offence.

clue.text: Uprising about to supplant popular revival

indicators.note: one short piece ousts another and takes its place in the word

parts.note: an insurrection is a revolt or uprising
in means fashionable or popular
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A rebellion against popular rule returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to supplant' swaps IN at the front of INSURRECTION for RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A resurrection is a return to life or use, a revival.

clue.text: Ability to reinforce a boundary

parts.note: touch means skill or knack, as in a deft touch
to line a garment is to strengthen it with an inner layer

explanation.surface: Talent is needed to shore up a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The touchline marks the side edge of a football or rugby pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby the touchline is the side limit of the playing area.

clue.text: Woody's ex, confronted by film classification, beginning to laugh and cry

parts.note: Mia Farrow was Woody Allen's former partner
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: the beginning of the word, its opening letter

explanation.surface: An actress meets a children's film rating and goes from laughter to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laugh and cry' looks like a single phrase, but 'cry' alone is the definition, a cat's mew.
explanation.definitionFit: To miaul is to mew like a cat, a feline cry.

clue.text: RU delegation organised relaxation of rules

indicators.note: organised means put into a fresh order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby union team was arranged to loosen regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (Rugby Union) and DELEGATION together are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Deregulation removes or eases official controls on an industry or market.

clue.text: A question could generate corrections to compensate for errors

indicators.note: generating here means creating something new from the same letters, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking something might lead to fixes for mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: An equation in astronomy or observation (the 'personal equation') is an allowance made for a known error.
explanation.definitionFit: In science an equation can mean an adjustment applied to offset a systematic inaccuracy, as with the personal equation of an observer.

clue.text: What's a group of cells? It's on the tip of my tongue

definitions.text: It's on the tip of my tongue

explanation.surface: A biology question, then someone groping for a word they almost remember.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as the idiom for nearly remembering something, but it is literal: the sensors sit on the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensory organ on the tongue is a small cluster of receptor cells, and many are found at its tip.

clue.text: Function involving extremists belonging to political party

indicators.note: the function's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
NF is the National Front, a far-right British group
in means belonging to, as in in the team

explanation.surface: An event attended by fanatics affiliated with a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a social event but is the maths sine; 'involving' puts NF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinn Féin is an Irish republican party active in Northern Ireland and the Republic.

clue.text: Beekeeper is a sanctimonious devotee of refined taste

parts.note: pi is a slang shortening of pious, meaning sanctimonious
a culturist is someone devoted to culture

explanation.surface: An apiarist turns out to be a smug aesthete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is the raising of bees, so one who practises it keeps hives.

clue.text: Maybe Dawn regularly stripped for Lenny Henry, grasping comic's bottom

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so one piece goes inside the other
stripping letters regularly removes every other one, keeping the first, third and so on

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Dawn stands in for Lenny Henry, holding on to the comic's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a British comedian, once married to Lenny Henry; 'Henry' gives only H, the unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn French is an English comic actress, so the surname is an example of a Dawn.

clue.text: Back in a tick

explanation.surface: Return shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it, and a moment or instant is also a second.

clue.text: Doctrine initially expounded in tabernacle

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the tent

parts.note: a tabernacle was a portable tent-like sanctuary

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Teaching first set out in a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes E from 'expounded', which 'in' puts inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true by a group.

clue.text: Potential winner taking speed and heroin

parts.note: to race is to speed
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A doped champion: a contender on speed and heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' links the pieces, and 'speed' and 'heroin' read as drugs on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred entered in a race could come first, so it may be a winner.

clue.text: Scavenger longing for the heart to laugh

indicators.note: the longing serves as the heart, the middle, of the other word

parts.note: ha is a laugh
a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: A carrion-eater yearns to laugh heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the heart' puts YEN in the middle of HA. The hyena is famous for its laugh-like call.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas feed largely on carrion left by other predators, the classic carrion feeder.

clue.text: Frenchman in stereotypical headgear suffering first European restriction

indicators.note: restriction means a cut, so a letter is taken away from the hat

parts.note: a beret is the hat stereotypically worn by a Frenchman

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European; first says the earlier of its two E's goes
to have a hat on is to be in it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in a beret is having trouble with European red tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' is a link word. 'first European' tells you which of the hat's two E's goes, and 'in' means wearing, as in having a hat on.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton is a native of Brittany in north-western France.

clue.text: Overlook present of new toy that is incomplete

parts.note: to give is to present
o is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

indicators.note: incomplete means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ignore the gift of an unfinished new plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlook' means look out over, as a window that faces a view, not to ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that faces a garden is said to look out on it, the sense of a window facing a view.

clue.text: Meal including a pastry

indicators.note: the meal holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a dish is a course or meal
an is the form of the article a before a vowel

explanation.surface: A meal featuring a sweet bun.
explanation.walkthrough: A Danish is a sweet yeast pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a flaky sweet bun, short for Danish pastry.

clue.text: Third of cheques new accountant lost converted into money

indicators.note: the third letter of the following word

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
shed means lost, as with leaves or weight

explanation.surface: An accountant mislaid a third of the new cheques after cashing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third of' picks E from cheques.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash a cheque is to cash it, exchanging it for banknotes.
